articles.title: Logic
articles.definition: Logic studies valid reasoning and formal systems for representing and assessing arguments. A formal logic typically specifies a language, a deductive system and/or model-theoretic semantics.
articles.scope_note: General reference summary; it does not imply every natural-language utterance is already formalized.

articles.title: First-order logic
articles.definition: A formal language with names, predicates, variables and quantifiers over individuals; consequence is assessed against a defined syntax and semantics.
articles.scope_note: Variables over individuals differ from quantification over properties or predicates.

articles.title: Second-order logic
articles.definition: An extension of first-order logic that may quantify over properties, relations or sets, depending on the formulation and semantics.
articles.scope_note: Higher-level architecture is not, by itself, a formal definition of second-order logic; the chosen semantics matter.

articles.title: Formal language
articles.definition: A vocabulary and grammar formally determining which strings are well-formed. Meaning and validity require an interpretation or semantic system beyond syntax alone.
articles.scope_note: Syntax validity does not by itself establish truth, meaning in a target domain, or empirical support.

articles.title: Deduction
articles.definition: A rule-governed relation in which a conclusion follows from stated premises within a specified logical system.
articles.scope_note: Validity does not independently authenticate the premises or their sources.

articles.title: Logical semantics
articles.definition: Interpretation of a formal language, often including satisfaction, truth in a model, and logical consequence.
articles.scope_note: WANGA relational and fractal semantics remain a research programme, not an established consequence of classical model theory.

articles.title: Metalogic
articles.definition: Study of formal logical systems themselves, including soundness, completeness, consistency, decidability and expressive power.
articles.scope_note: A system describing itself is not automatically sound or complete; such properties require definitions and proofs.

articles.title: Evidence and provenance
articles.definition: A record of where a claim or model component came from, which exact source span supports it, which transformations were applied, and which checks were performed.
articles.scope_note: A URL establishes a reference location, not proof that the source supports a particular claim. BUILT, TESTED and VERIFIED are separate states.

articles.title: Source-first-before-weights contract
articles.definition: The WANGA project rule that source lineage, literal extraction, semantic structure, relation extraction, first-order and second-order review, and closure checks precede configuration and weights.
articles.scope_note: A project contract, not a theorem of general logic. Reconcile against the canonical current contract file before execution.

articles.title: Logical fractal
articles.definition: A proposed recursively composable logical structure in which validated primitives and relations form substructures that can be composed into higher-level structures while preserving constraints, provenance and counterexample results.
articles.scope_note: Self-similarity or geometric fractality alone does not establish logical validity. Grammar, composition operators and invariant-preservation conditions remain to be formalized.

articles.title: Fractal composition rule
articles.definition: A candidate rule that composes logical structures into a new structure while declaring input types, preconditions, output type, preserved invariants, source provenance and failure cases.
articles.scope_note: Composition is rejected when required relations or premises are missing; numeric weights cannot manufacture absent edges.

articles.title: Logical primitive
articles.definition: The smallest declared unit in a particular WANGA logic model, with a stable identifier, type, source or explicit assumption, contract and tests.
articles.scope_note: There is no established universal primitive count for the proposed WANGA system; counts must come from an audited corpus.

articles.title: Logical relation
articles.definition: A typed connection among declared components or propositions with explicit direction, arity, scope, source support and applicability conditions.
articles.scope_note: A graph edge, co-occurrence or numerical similarity is not automatically a valid logical relation.

articles.title: Logic-Native Language (LNL)
articles.definition: A prototype declarative language with source, fact, rule, goal and constraint statements; its compiler produces a model graph and execution bundle for the WANGA symbolic kernel.
articles.scope_note: LNL/0.1 is a small typed syntax; it is not a trained model and does not formalize arbitrary natural language.

articles.title: MLN continuous field
articles.definition: A research prototype for continuous M/L/N measurement fields and a relational operator, with smoothing, spectral/topological diagnostics and conservative sandbox updates.
articles.scope_note: The archived/local implementation is a numerical proxy. Scale normalization and the golden-balance expression are not established laws of intelligence.

articles.title: First model readiness gate
articles.definition: Explicit source-coverage, primitive, composition, counterexample, benchmark, reproducibility and review requirements before releasing the first Logic Fractal Alpha candidate.
articles.scope_note: Thresholds are provisional project policy; passing permits candidate review, not a claim of AGI or universal correctness.

articles.title: Logic Wiki
articles.definition: A version-controlled research encyclopedia connecting stable concept IDs to sources, claims, primitives, relation maps, composition rules, tests, model versions and uncertainty statuses.
articles.scope_note: This is an original project encyclopedia, not an official Wikipedia project.

articles.title: Typed logic fragment
articles.definition: A bounded logical fragment with a stable ID, scale, typed inputs/outputs, claims, source-span IDs, provenance, tests, counterexamples and a composition contract.
articles.scope_note: Type compatibility supports composition but does not establish semantic equivalence. A composite fragment becomes CANDIDATE until source review and benchmark tests pass.

articles.title: Logical particle
articles.definition: A proposed smallest typed unit in the WANGA logical-fractal representation. It may carry a primitive or relation together with type, interface, source lineage, scope and test references.
articles.scope_note: The word particle is an engineering metaphor, not a physical claim and not proof that this unit is the universal atom of logic. Unit boundaries require source-grounded semantics and counterexamples.

articles.title: Fractal composition invariant
articles.definition: A condition intended to remain true when validated logical fragments are composed at a higher scale, such as typed interface compatibility, stable parent IDs, source lineage, and preserved constraints.
articles.scope_note: An invariant must be stated as an executable predicate with positive and negative tests. Similar shapes, shared terms, or successful serialization are not semantic proof.

articles.title: Recursive logical composition
articles.definition: A multi-scale operation that composes previously validated candidate fragments into a higher-level candidate while preserving the full parent graph, contracts, tests, and provenance.
articles.scope_note: Each composition remains a candidate until semantic and counterexample tests pass. Recursion cannot silently upgrade a component or an editorial link into logical entailment.

articles.title: Conversation evidence unit
articles.definition: A source-scoped record produced from an explicitly provided conversation export, preserving available conversation/message identifiers, parent links, dates, content segments and hashes for private review.
articles.scope_note: The intake tool only processes exports supplied to it. It does not grant automatic access to all private ChatGPT history. Raw exports are not published to GitHub or Wix; only reviewed, permissioned and redacted derivatives may be public.

articles.title: Counterexample case
articles.definition: A controlled input and expected limiting or failing outcome designed to challenge a rule, composition, interpretation or model candidate.
articles.scope_note: Unit tests for software contracts are not semantic ground-truth benchmarks. A counterexample must state its source, target claim/rule, expected result, reviewer and adjudication status.

articles.title: Bounded autonomous research agent
articles.definition: A bounded work unit with explicit inputs, outputs, evidence requirements and stop conditions, such as source collection, extraction, composition, adversarial review, benchmarking or wiki curation.
articles.scope_note: A registered role is not itself an autonomous AI capability. Execution is claimed only when a run produces a report; access gaps, failures and blocked work must be recorded.

articles.title: Multi-scale logical-fractal map
articles.definition: A versioned map connecting logical units and composed fragments across scales, with stable IDs, typed edges, parent links, provenance, constraints, counterexamples and status metadata.
articles.scope_note: Keep an editorial knowledge graph separate from an executable composition graph. A link denotes navigation or a proposed relationship unless a rule contract and evidence establish a stronger relation.

articles.title: Longitudinal logic research cycle
articles.definition: A repeatable process that checks available sources, registers new evidence, extracts and normalizes logic, composes candidates, runs adversarial and benchmark checks, evaluates readiness, generates a dated report and updates approved public summaries.
articles.scope_note: Scheduled runs operate only on accessible inputs and connected tools. They cannot fetch private conversation history unless an export is provided. A no-change, blocked or failed run is a valid result; publication requires source/provenance checks and Wix read-back.

articles.title: Logical diamond
articles.definition: A project hypothesis that a logic asset can be treated as a reusable multi-facet structure: source extraction, configuration, composition, drift testing, fit boundaries, use contexts and versioned validation.
articles.scope_note: Diamond is a design metaphor/hypothesis here, not an established mathematical object or accepted universal law. Future work must define each facet as an operation or invariant, specify relations between facets, and test whether composition preserves meaning and scope.

articles.title: ARK-Swarm and Logic Trader
articles.definition: A bounded coordinator that connects the Logic Wiki catalog, candidate fractal composer, typed-fragment checks, source-provenance gate, counter-reading candidate, and existing six-role agent integration suite. The Logic Trader ranks assets by lexical overlap and source/link metadata, assembles an internal candidate logic package, and preserves source IDs and hashes.
articles.scope_note: Lexical ranking is not semantic relevance. The runtime is local and deterministic; P2P transport, replicated network CRDTs, biological connectome execution, external model calls, and automatic release are not implemented.
